implementation.notes: Screenshot at scroll=0 confirms real photo layers composite with correct depth and title legible. Source art has a baked-in FIREWATCH wordmark behind the title (part of parallax PNGs). Optional floating 3D model deferred to WS2.
implementation.summary: Replaced the procedural SVG mountains/sun/fog in HeroSection.tsx with the 9 real Firewatch PNG layers (parallax0 back/sky .. parallax8 front/trees), stacked z-0..z-8 inside absolute-inset wrappers rendered object-cover and oversized ~110% via negative inset (-inset-[5%], not a scale class) so scroll+mouse parallax never expose edges. Reused the existing single-rAF native-scroll+pointer engine that owns each layer's inline translate3d; data-speed ramps back 0.0 -> front 0.55, data-depth back 2 -> front 26. parallax0 eager (LCP, fetchPriority high); rest lazy. PRADIPTA JANA identity + role cycler overlaid at z-20 with gentle data-speed=0.12/data-depth=0.6. Reduced-motion early-returns from rAF (static first frame). Removed dead .hero-sun/.hero-stars CSS and unused RidgeLayer/FogBand/Watchtower/PRNG code. No Lenis, no new ScrollTrigger pin.

feedback: Baked-in FIREWATCH wordmark in the source art shows behind the title (cosmetic source-asset artifact); consider masking the art or nudging the title if a cleaner composition is wanted.

9 full-bleed 7000x2076 images: watch decode/memory in the WS5 perf pass; consider downscaled/responsive sources.
review.summary: WS1 meets all acceptance criteria. HeroSection.tsx renders the 9 real Firewatch photographic PNG layers (parallax0 sky/back .. parallax8 trees/front) as elements (not SVG), z-stacked 0..8 in correct depth order. The rAF engine exclusively owns each layer's inline transform (wrappers oversize via -inset-[5%], no transform utility classes), honoring the guardrail. Mouse + scroll parallax wired via single rAF reading native scrollY (capped) + pointermove; no Lenis, no GSAP pin. Reduced-motion returns early. PRADIPTA JANA overlays at z-20, legible with drop-shadow. Role-cycler span has no React children (no textContent crash). tsc --noEmit exits 0.

implementation.notes: Gate moved from pre-existing 1024px to spec'd 768px. Pin target is an inner static div (not the section) since SectionFrame wraps with overflow-hidden+padding. Screenshot at scrollY ~6562 confirms mid-pin horizontal offset (slide 01 off-screen left, 03/04/05 visible, 04 centred+scaled) + bottom rail. Waited out the SYS.PRELOAD overlay before scrolling.
implementation.summary: Implemented WS3 horizontal-scroll pin. Project cards render as a STATIC horizontal flex track inside a pin target (md:h-[100svh], md:overflow-hidden). useEffect after registerAll() runs a gsap.context() scoped to rootRef with gsap.matchMedia() guarded to '(min-width:768px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)' — the only GSAP pin in the app. Tweens track x to -(track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), ease none, scrollTrigger { trigger pinRef, start top top, end +=amount, pin:true, scrub:1, anticipatePin:1, invalidateOnRefresh:true }. onUpdate drives a bottom progress rail (scaleX) and per-slide entrance (scale 0.86->1, opacity 0.4->1 by distance from centre). matchMedia cleanup kills trigger/tween + clearProps; context reverted on unmount. Below 768px / reduced-motion = vertical stacked cards, no pin. Real project data reused from content/projects.ts.

feedback: Minor: per-slide onUpdate gsap.set runs every frame for every slide; a quickSetter would be marginally cheaper (defer to WS5).
Edge case: amount() returns 0 if track.scrollWidth <= innerWidth (very wide viewport, few cards) -> end becomes +=0 and pin collapses; add a min scroll distance guard (defer to WS5).
review.summary: WS3 Projects horizontal-scroll pin fully meets the plan. Section pins a static track via a single GSAP ScrollTrigger (pin:true, scrub:1) translating x to -(scrollWidth-innerWidth); gsap.matchMedia() gates the pin to (min-width:768px)+no-preference with a vertical stacked-card fallback below; per-slide scale/opacity entrance + bottom progress rail driven by horizontal progress; cleanup via matchMedia teardown + gsap.context().revert(). Mid-scroll screenshot shows real horizontal offset (Admin Dashboard centred, neighbours clipped). tsc clean. Only GSAP pin; pinned subtree never re-renders.

implementation.notes: tsc --noEmit exits 0. THREE screenshots captured (ws2_a hero / ws2_b ~35% / ws2_c ~65%) but the helmet does NOT appear: documented headless-GPU limitation, NOT a code failure. Headless chromium SwiftShader -> getGPUTier() in lib/usePerfTier.ts classifies renderer as 'low' -> SceneContainer renders SvgCoreFallback and the ambient WebGL Canvas never mounts (diagnostic: 0 canvas elements, 0 GLB requests). GLB serves HTTP 200 (3.77MB). On a real GPU the canvas mounts and the helmet travels/lands per section. The fallback behaving this way also confirms the gating guardrail is intact. NEEDS real-GPU browser verification by the user.
implementation.summary: Implemented WS2 traveling 3D model. Extended ScenePose with pos[x,y,z]/rot[x,y,z]/scale per section + matching ScenePoseTarget fields (pos/rot as Vector3, scale number), makePoseTarget, and component-wise lerp in samplePose. Per-section waypoints trace hero(up/right near sun) -> about(close/left) -> skills(orbit right) -> projects(recede high/back) -> experience(orbit left) -> contact(centred). Created TravelerModel.tsx: useGLTF('/models/DamagedHelmet.glb') + preload, clones scene, each frame reads sceneStore.progress + samplePose and THREE.MathUtils.damp's group position/rotation/scale toward target (same pattern as CameraController, slightly slower so it trails the camera) + subtle sin idle bob + slow Y spin; drei Environment+Lightformers light the PBR helmet. Mounted in Scene.tsx beside ParticleField inside the existing single Suspense. No second pause mechanism: model shares the canvas whose frameloop flips to 'never' on portfolio:bg-pause (one canvas active at a time). SceneContainer/SvgCoreFallback gating intact.

feedback: Allocation-free per-frame (memoized target mutated in place, memoized clone, frame-rate-independent spin/bob, dt clamped to 0.05 like CameraController).
Pause correct by design: relies on shared canvas frameloop flipping to never (no conflicting second mechanism).
NEEDS real-GPU browser verification by the user (headless cannot render the WebGL canvas).
review.summary: WS2 correctly implemented, matching the existing render-loop damp pattern. A single persistent TravelerModel loads DamagedHelmet.glb via drei useGLTF (+preload) inside the shared canvas Suspense alongside ParticleField, damps toward samplePose(progress) every frame via THREE.MathUtils.damp exactly like CameraController, layers idle bob + slow spin, and inherits portfolio:bg-pause via the shared frameloop:'never' in _Scene.tsx. ScenePose/ScenePoseTarget/samplePose extended consistently with pos/rot/scale for all 6 poses, allocation-free, no NaN paths. SceneContainer/SvgCoreFallback gating untouched. tsc exits 0. Headless visual limitation is expected and does not affect the verdict.
